calls.reason: No deadline was given and there is no agreed measure for either side of the condition. The best agent scoring 30% on TheAgentCompany and OpenAI calling its agent early-stage show agents still fall short, but that leaves the forecast open.
PolyMATH documents ongoing spatial errors but does not show why they keep appearing. The Sparkle study finds some fixes do generalize, so the causal explanation is neither established nor ruled out.

The packet has only one Disney example and one NASA example plus a narrow lab result on intuitive physics. Nothing actually compares how well simulation works across these domains, so 'much less effective' is not shown either way.

Independent 2024 studies found LLMs weak at spatial reasoning (SpaRC) and video models failing physical commonsense (PhyGenBench). Simulation's successes were narrow tasks, so none of the three approaches looked fully satisfactory.

This is a necessity claim that can only be tested once agents become reliable. In late 2025 the best agents completed 30% of TheAgentCompany tasks and 2.5% of Remote Labor Index projects, so that hasn't happened yet.

OpenAI's technical report says Sora decodes latents to pixels without explicit object or 3D biases. Its December 2024 launch post admits Sora often generates unrealistic physics, an admission against its own interest.
